plan: Deuteronomy 16:18–17:13; Deuteronomy 17:14-20; Deuteronomy 18:1-8, 9-14, 15-22; Deuteronomy 19:1-13, 14-21; Deuteronomy 20:1-20; Deuteronomy 21:1-9

readings.title: Appointing Judges and Purging Evil
readings.subtitle: The Administration of Righteous Right-Ruling
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 16:18] “Appoint judges and officers within all your gates, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, according to your tribes. And they shall judge <dn>את</dn> the people with righteous right-ruling. [19] Do not distort right-ruling. Do not show partiality, nor take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of the righteous. [20] Follow righteousness, righteousness alone, so that you live and inherit <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you. [21] Do not plant for yourself any tree as an Ashěrah near the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> that you make for yourself. [22] And do not set up a pillar, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> hates. [Deuteronomy 17:1] Do not slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> a bull or sheep which has any blemish, any evil matter, for that is an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [2] When there is found in your midst, in any of your cities which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, a man or a woman who does <dn>את</dn> what is evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, in transgressing <dn>His</dn> covenant, [3] and has gone and served other mighty ones and bowed down to them, or to the sun or to the moon or to any of the host of the heavens, which <dn>I</dn> have not commanded, [4] and it has been made known to you and you have heard, and have searched diligently. Then see, if true: the matter is confirmed that such an abomination has been done in Yisra’ěl, [5] then you shall bring out to your gates <dn>את</dn> that man or <dn>את</dn> woman who has done <dn>את</dn> this evil matter, and you shall stone to death <dn>את</dn> that man or <dn>את</dn> woman with stones. [6] At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall he that is to die be put to death. <dn>He</dn> is not put to death by the mouth of one witness. [7] The hand of the witnesses shall be first against him to put him to death, and the hand of all the people last. So you shall purge the evil from your midst. [8] When any matter arises which is too hard for you to judge, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, or between stroke and stroke – matters of strife within your gates – then you shall rise and go up to the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses, [9] and shall come to the priests, the Lěvites, and to the judge who is in those days, and shall inquire. And they shall declare to you <dn>את</dn> the word of right-ruling, [10] and you shall do according to the word which they declare to you from that place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses. And you shall guard to do according to all that they instruct you. [11] Do according to the Torah in which they teach you, according to the right-ruling which they say to you. You do not turn to the right or to the left from the word which they declare to you. [12] And the man who acts arrogantly, so as not to listen to the priest who stands to serve there before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, or to the judge, that man shall die. So you shall purge the evil from Yisra’ěl. [13] And let all the people hear and fear, and no longer do arrogantly.”

readings.title: The Sovereign of Yisra'el
readings.subtitle: Guarding the Words of the Torah
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 17:14] “When you come to the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, and shall possess it and shall dwell in it, and you shall say, ‘Let me set a sovereign over me like all the nations that are around me,’ [15] you shall certainly set a sovereign over you whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall choose. Set a sovereign over you from among your brothers, you are not allowed to set a foreigner over you, who is not your brother. [16] Only, he is not to increase horses for himself, nor cause <dn>את</dn> the people to return to Mitsrayim to increase horses, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has said to you, <dq>‘Do not return that way again.’</dq> [17] And he is not to increase wives for himself, lest his heart turn away, nor is he to greatly increase silver and gold for himself. [18] And it shall be, when he sits on the throne of his reign, that he shall write for himself <dn>את</dn> a copy of this Torah in a book, from the one before the priests, the Lěvites. [19] And it shall be with him, and he shall read it all the days of his life, so that he learns to fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> and guard <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah and <dn>את</dn> these laws, to do them, [20] so that his heart is not lifted up above his brothers, and so as not to turn aside from the command, right or left, so that he prolongs his days in his reign, he and his children, in the midst of Yisra’ěl.”

readings.title: The Portion of the Priests
readings.subtitle: The Inheritance of Levi
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 18:1] “The priests, the Lěvites, all the tribe of Lěvi, have no part nor inheritance with Yisra’ěl. They are to eat the offerings of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made by fire, and <dn>His</dn> inheritance. [2] But among his brothers Lěvi has no inheritance. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is his inheritance, as <dn>He</dn> has spoken to him. [3] And this is the priest’s right from the people, from those who slaughter a slaughtering, whether it is bull or sheep: they shall give to the priest the shoulder, and the two cheeks, and the stomach; [4] the first-fruits of your grain and your new wine and your oil, and the first of the fleece of your sheep, you give to him. [5] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has chosen him out of all your tribes to stand to serve in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, him and his sons forever. [6] And when the Lěvite comes from one of your gates, from where he has sojourned among all Yisra’ěl, and shall come with all the desire of his being to the place which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> chooses, [7] then he shall serve in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn>, like all his brothers the Lěvites, who are standing there before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [8] They are to have portion for portion to eat, besides what comes from the sale of his inheritance.”

readings.title: Abominations of the Nations
readings.subtitle: Prohibition of Divination and Magic
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 18:9] “When you come into the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, do not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations. [10] Let no one be found among you who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, or one who practises divination, or a user of magic, or one who interprets omens or a sorcerer, [11] or one who conjures spells, or a medium, or a spiritist, or one who calls up the dead. [12] For whoever does these is an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and because of these abominations <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> drives them out from before you. [13] Be perfect before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, [14] for these nations whom you are possessing do listen to those using magic and to diviners. But as for you, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has not appointed such for you.”

readings.title: The Prophet Like Moses
readings.subtitle: The Promise of the Right Arm
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 18:15] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall raise up for you a Prophet like me from your midst, from your brothers. Listen to <dn>Him</dn>, [16] according to all you asked of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> in Ḥorěḇ in the day of the assembly, saying, ‘Let me not hear again <dn>את</dn> the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, nor let me see <dn>את</dn> this great fire any more, lest I die.’ [17] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘What they have spoken is good.</dq> [18] <dq><dn>I</dn> shall raise up for them a Prophet like you out of the midst of their brothers. And <dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>My</dn> Words in <dn>His</dn> mouth, and <dn>He</dn> shall speak to them <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>I</dn> command <dn>Him</dn>.</dq> [19] <dq>And it shall be, the man who does not listen to <dn>My</dn> Words which <dn>He</dn> speaks in <dn>My</dn> Name, <dn>I</dn> require it of him.</dq> [20] <dq>But the prophet who presumes to speak a word in <dn>My</dn> Name, <dn>את</dn> which <dn>I</dn> have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other mighty ones, even that prophet shall die.’</dq> [21] And when you say in your heart, ‘How do we know <dn>את</dn> the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not spoken?’ – [22] when the prophet speaks in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the word is not, or comes not, that is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.”

readings.title: Cities of Refuge
readings.subtitle: Protection from the Revenger of Blood
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 19:1] “When <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> cuts off <dn>את</dn> the nations whose land <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, and you dispossess them and dwell in their cities and in their houses, [2] separate three cities for yourself in the midst of your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to possess. [3] Prepare a way for yourself, and divide into three parts <dn>את</dn> the border of your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to inherit, that any man-slayer shall flee there. [4] And this matter of the man-slayer who flees there and lives: he who strikes <dn>את</dn> his neighbour unknowingly, not having hated him in time past, [5] even he who goes to the forest with his neighbour to cut timber, and his hand swings a stroke with the axe to cut down the tree, and the head slips from the handle and strikes <dn>את</dn> his neighbour so that he dies – let him flee to one of these cities and live, [6] lest the revenger of blood, while his displeasure is hot, pursue the man-slayer and overtake him, because the way is long, and shall strike his being, though he was not worthy of death, since he had not hated him before. [7] Therefore I am commanding you, saying, ‘Separate three cities for yourself.’ [8] And if <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> enlarges <dn>את</dn> your border, as <dn>He</dn> swore to your fathers, and has given you <dn>את</dn> all the land which <dn>He</dn> promised to give to your fathers – [9] when you guard <dn>את</dn> all this command to do it, which I am commanding you today, to love <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and to walk in <dn>His</dn> ways all the days – then you shall add three more cities for yourself besides these three, [10] so that innocent blood is not shed in the midst of your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you as an inheritance, or blood-guilt shall be upon you. [11] But when anyone hates his neighbour, and shall lie in wait for him and rise against him and strike his being so that he dies, then he shall flee to one of these cities, [12] and the elders of his city shall send and bring him from there, and give him into the hand of the revenger of blood, and he shall die. [13] Your eye shall not pardon him, but you shall purge the blood of innocent blood from Yisra’ěl, so that it might be well with you.”

readings.title: Witnesses and Boundaries
readings.subtitle: Establishing Matters by Two or Three
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 19:14] “Do not remove your neighbour’s boundary, which those in the past have set, in your inheritance which you inherit in the land that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to possess. [15] One witness does not rise up against a man concerning any crookedness or any sin that he commits. At the mouth of two witnesses or at the mouth of three witnesses a matter is established. [16] When a malicious witness rises up against any man to accuse him of turning aside, [17] then both men who have the dispute shall stand before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, before the priests and the judges who serve in those days. [18] And the judges shall diligently search and see if the witness is a false witness, who has falsely accused his brother, [19] then you shall do to him as he thought to have done to his brother. Thus you shall purge the evil from your midst. [20] And let the rest hear and fear, and never again do this evil matter in your midst. [21] And let your eye not pardon, life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.”

readings.title: Laws of Warfare
readings.subtitle: Trusting YeHoVaH in Battle
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 20:1] “When you go out to battle against your enemies, and shall see horses and chariots and people more numerous than you, do not be afraid of them, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought you up from the land of Mitsrayim, is with you. [2] And it shall be, when you draw near to the battle, that the priest shall come and speak to the people, [3] and shall say to them, ‘Hear, O Yisra’ěl: You are drawing near today to battle with your enemies. Do not let your heart faint, do not fear, or tremble, or be afraid before them, [4] for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is <dn>He</dn> who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save <dn>את</dn> you.’ [5] And the officers shall speak to the people, saying, ‘Who is the man who has built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man dedicate it. [6] And who is the man who has planted a vineyard and has not begun to use it? Let him also go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man should begin to use it. [7] And who is the man who is engaged to a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her.’ [8] And the officers shall speak further to the people, and say, ‘Who is the man who is afraid and tender of heart? Let him go and return to his house, lest the heart of his brothers faint like his heart.’ [9] And it shall be, when the officers have finished speaking to the people, that they shall appoint commanders of the divisions to lead the people. [10] When you draw near to a city to fight against it, then you shall make a call for peace to it. [11] And it shall be that if it accepts your call for peace, and shall open to you, then all the people found in it are to be your compulsory labour, and serve you. [12] But if it does not make peace with you, and shall fight against you, then you shall besiege it, [13] and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall give it into your hands, and you shall strike <dn>את</dn> every male in it with the edge of the sword. [14] Only the women, and the little ones, and the livestock, and all that is in the city, all its spoil, you take as plunder for yourself. And you shall eat <dn>את</dn> the enemies’ plunder which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> gives you. [15] Do so to all the cities which are very far from you, which are not of the cities of these nations. [16] Only, of the cities of these peoples which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> gives you as an inheritance, you do not keep alive any that breathe, [17] but you shall certainly put them under the ban: the Ḥittite and the Amorite and the Kena‛anite and the Perizzite and the Ḥivvite and the Yeḇusite, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has commanded you, [18] lest they teach <dn>את</dn> you to do according to all their abominations which they have done for their mighty ones, and you sin against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [19] When you besiege a city for a long time by fighting against it to take it, you do not destroy <dn>את</dn> its trees by wielding an axe against them. If you do eat of them, do not cut them down. For is the tree of the field a man to be besieged by you? [20] Only the trees which you know are not trees for food you do destroy and cut down, to build siege-works against the city that is fighting against you, until it falls.”

readings.title: The Unsolved Murder
readings.subtitle: Purging the Guilt of Innocent Blood
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 21:1] “When anyone is found slain, lying in the field in the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you to possess, and it is not known who struck him, [2] then your elders and your judges shall go out, and they shall measure the distance from the slain man to the cities round about. [3] And it shall be that the elders of the city nearest to the slain man shall take a heifer which has not been worked and which has not pulled with a yoke, [4] and the elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a wadi with flowing water, which is neither ploughed nor sown, and they shall break the heifer’s neck there in the wadi. [5] And the priests, the sons of Lěvi, shall come near, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has chosen them to serve <dn>Him</dn> and to bless in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and by their mouth every strife and every stroke is tried. [6] And let all the elders of that city nearest to the slain man wash <dn>את</dn> their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the wadi. [7] And they shall answer and say, ‘Our hands have not shed <dn>את</dn> this blood, nor have our eyes seen it. [8] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, forgive <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl, whom <dn>You</dn> have ransomed, and do not allow innocent blood in the midst of <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’ěl.’ And the blood-guilt shall be pardoned to them. [9] Thus you purge the guilt of innocent blood from your midst when you do what is right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”
